reading.body:
CyrusOne Sterling provides 44 MW across three linked facilities in Northern Virginia, translating to approximately 1,100 racks at standard AI training density and ranking 12th among Virginia's 25 disclosed data center locations.

The facility's 2.6 MW per 10,000 square feet suggests mixed workload support rather than optimization for high-density accelerator clusters. Its compliance certifications cover financial services, health data, federal contracting, and infrastructure standards, fitting the profile of a general-purpose colocation operator. Sterling represents 2.7% of Virginia's published 1,603 MW, though only 25 of the state's 330 mapped data center locations publish power data, making disclosure itself rare.

At 44 MW, Sterling's capacity can support a modest model training pipeline or mid-scale inference deployment but falls below the 100+ MW scale of purpose-built AI campuses now competing for grid resources. Whether this site constrains or enables large-scale AI workloads depends entirely on factors not disclosed here: CyrusOne's grid interconnection agreements, power procurement contracts, and whether Virginia's broader transmission capacity permits expansion at this location.
